items.questionAndWhy: Does the anterior cingulate cortex generate a brain signal related to goal feedback?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers compared lesion locations with EEG reward-positivity signals in 68 stroke patients doing a trial-and-error task.
items.whatTheyFound: Damage to a caudal anterior cingulate area weakened the signal. The lesion evidence supports its role in generating reward positivity, not a complete account of motivation.
items.whatItMeans: Brain-lesion evidence helps localize an EEG process but does not demonstrate effects on everyday goal pursuit.
items.streamTitle: Stroke lesions weaken a brain signal linked to goal feedback
items.streamSummary: EEG in 68 stroke patients linked caudal anterior cingulate damage with weaker reward-positivity signals. Neural localization does not establish broad motivational outcomes.

items.questionAndWhy: Does a changing maze slow problem solving or also stop people learning the optimal strategy?
items.whatTheyDid: A 132-person virtual-maze experiment compared fixed layouts with layouts changing across trials as participants searched for hidden coins.
items.whatTheyFound: Both groups improved; changing layouts slowed gains in route efficiency and completion time. A difference in optimal-strategy learning did not survive multiple-testing correction.
items.whatItMeans: Changing environments can slow task execution without clearly impairing underlying rule learning.
items.streamTitle: Changing mazes slowed navigation, not clearly rule learning
items.streamSummary: A virtual-maze study of 132 people showed reduced gains in route and time efficiency under changing layouts. The optimal-rule learning difference was inconclusive.

items.questionAndWhy: Can AI agents discover hidden rules in social dilemmas and still cooperate over time?
items.whatTheyDid: OpenSocialJax tested eight language models in changing resource-harvest and cleanup games, using five repeated trials per hidden setting.
items.whatTheyFound: Rule discovery often improved play but did not ensure cooperation. Cleanup became concentrated among fewer agents; every tested team eventually depleted the shared harvest resource.
items.whatItMeans: Environmental understanding does not guarantee collective action. These benchmark outcomes describe AI agents, not human behavior.
items.streamTitle: AI agents learned hidden game rules but still exhausted common resources
items.streamSummary: OpenSocialJax found eight language models could learn environmental rules yet failed to sustain cooperation in shared-resource tasks. The results are simulations of agents, not human evidence.

items.questionAndWhy: Do added input perturbations improve forecasting and produce calibrated uncertainty intervals?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers tested four simulated-noise approaches with random-forest groundwater forecasts, comparing point errors and the coverage of nominal 95% intervals.
items.whatTheyFound: None improved baseline prediction accuracy. Wider intervals gave better coverage, but no configuration reached 95%; the highest reported coverage was 83.6%.
items.whatItMeans: Synthetic prediction spread is not automatically reliable uncertainty. Assess accuracy, coverage and real measurement-error assumptions separately.
items.streamTitle: No tested input-noise method improved accuracy or reached 95% coverage
items.streamSummary: A groundwater forecasting experiment found accuracy–coverage trade-offs under simulated input noise. None improved baseline accuracy or achieved nominal interval coverage.

items.questionAndWhy: How can NATO turn documented lessons from exercises into actual organizational adaptation?
items.whatTheyDid: NATO's 2026 Lessons Learned Conference in Lisbon discussed interoperability, training, multi-domain operations and possible AI-assisted analysis.
items.whatTheyFound: The official report prioritized putting lessons into practice rather than collecting reports. It provided no quantitative evaluation of improved readiness or learning speed.
items.whatItMeans: Track the changes implemented and results achieved, not merely the number of observations captured.
items.streamTitle: NATO emphasizes implementing lessons rather than simply collecting them
items.streamSummary: The October 14 official conference account stressed converting operational observations into institutional action. It did not report demonstrated performance gains.
items.attribution: NATO Allied Command Transformation — official report

items.questionAndWhy: How does China's revised mineral law connect resource security, allocation and environmental duties?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers analyzed China's 2024 mineral law, used a document-based Guangxi case and compared institutional approaches in the EU and Australia.
items.whatTheyFound: They mapped contractual, financial and administrative mechanisms while identifying a gap between compliance requirements and demonstrated ecological outcomes.
items.whatItMeans: Legal design and early implementation are not evidence of successful policy effects. Track environmental and supply outcomes separately.
items.streamTitle: Mineral-law study distinguishes safeguards from demonstrated policy outcomes
items.streamSummary: A legal analysis finds tools linking mineral allocation, environmental obligations and strategic supply, but documents potential gaps between formal compliance and real outcomes.
items.attribution: Li et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.questionAndWhy: Do satellite measures of park cooling match how visitors describe thermal comfort?
items.whatTheyDid: Researchers combined remote-sensing measures in Shenzhen wetland parks with AI-coded thermal impressions from 11,109 online reviews.
items.whatTheyFound: Relationships were nonlinear: landscape variety related to cooling, while moderate path density related to cooler perceptions. Reported turning points were sample-specific.
items.whatItMeans: Objective conditions and subjective comfort are distinct. Self-selected reviews cannot establish effects of changing park design.
items.streamTitle: Park cooling and visitors' comfort reports followed different nonlinear patterns
items.streamSummary: A Shenzhen analysis linked satellite data to 11,109 public reviews. Physical and perceived cooling were not simply proportional; reported design thresholds are exploratory.
items.attribution: Zhao and Wang — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.questionAndWhy: Can a fast surrogate estimate evacuation delays after earthquake damage to bridges?
items.whatTheyDid: A model was trained on 100,000 traffic simulations of earthquakes affecting Pohang, South Korea's road network with 48 bridges.
items.whatTheyFound: The surrogate approximated simulation results with reported high accuracy and lower computation time. Larger and nearer earthquakes caused greater simulated delays.
items.whatItMeans: Agreement with a simulator supports faster scenario analysis but does not establish accuracy against actual evacuations.
items.streamTitle: Fast evacuation model trained on 100,000 simulated earthquake scenarios
items.streamSummary: Using 48 bridges in a real city network, researchers built a faster approximation of simulated evacuation time. Real-world evacuation outcomes were not validated.
